description: This donut chart visually compares the distribution of deception outcomes across two levels of ambiguity, labeled “Ambiguity 1 (Outer)” and “Ambiguity 2 (Inner)”, each broken down into three categories: “Deceived” (red), “Partially” (yellow), and “Not Deceived” (green). The outer ring, representing Ambiguity 1, is divided into three segments: the largest red segment (“Deceived”) accounts for 67.6% of the outer ring, the yellow segment (“Partially”) is 57.9%, and the green segment (“Not Deceived”) is 31.6%. The inner ring, representing Ambiguity 2, is similarly divided: the red segment (“Deceived”) is 10.5%, the yellow segment (“Partially”) is 8.8%, and the green segment (“Not Deceived”) is 23.5%. Each percentage is labeled directly on its corresponding segment. The chart includes two legends, one for each ambiguity level, mapping the colors to their respective categories. The segments are arranged in a clockwise order from the top, with the largest segment starting at the top and proceeding clockwise.
